newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end with minor gains.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end with minor gains.

text.p: Swiss shares ended with minor gains on modest volumes after a quiet session marked by see-saw moves in the stock indices.
"Everybody is bearish, so there was little buying even at lower levels", one dealer said.
Investors were likely to hedge their bets on Friday ahead of U.S. employment figures and due to the fact that some markets such as those in Germany will remain closed for All Saints' Day.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index added 0.06 percent, or 2.2 points, to 3,725.3. Technical support around 3,700 points in the SMI may be tested in the next few days, a trader said.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 2.52 points, or 0.11 percent, to 2,393.84 points.
Thursday's U.S. economic data did not move the market much, a trader noted.
Actively-traded Nestle recovered from early weakness to end eight francs higher at 1,373 due to buying interest.
UBS stocks continued their recent weak streak and were among the biggest losers among blue chips. The bearer shares posted a slump of 1.23 percent to 1,204 francs.
Roche certificates stood out among pharmaceuticls with an advance of 35 francs to 9,560.
Swissair saw a turbulent session after Belgian carrier Sabena's CEO Paul Reutlinger hinted at the possibility that Swissair may write off its 49.5 percent stake in Sabena.
Swissair later said it had no plans to pull out of Sabena. News that Sabena pilots called off a strike helped the shares in late trade. Swissair stocks fell one franc to 985.

Sulzer shares jumped 1.27 percent to 719 francs after news that company planned a public offering for its subsidiary Elma Electronic AG. Investors may have interpreted the move as a sign that Sulzer is willing to restructure the group.
Temporary services group Adecco, which had outperformed the market recently, lost three percent to 355 francs after profit taking.
